title: PostgreSQL 18: Transactions
provenance: PostgreSQL Global Development Group, PostgreSQL 18 manual. Project-authored summary checked 2026-11-26.
text: A transaction groups related database operations into one unit. BEGIN opens an explicit transaction block and COMMIT makes its changes durable and visible to others. ROLLBACK discards the transaction's pending changes. When transferring funds between accounts, put both balance updates in the same transaction so a failure cannot leave only one update committed. SAVEPOINT marks a position inside a transaction. ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT discards changes after that position while allowing the enclosing transaction to continue.

title: PostgreSQL 18: Reading execution plans
provenance: PostgreSQL Global Development Group, PostgreSQL 18 manual. Project-authored summary checked 2026-11-26.
text: EXPLAIN displays the execution plan chosen by the query planner. The plan is a tree of operations such as scans, joins and sorts. Compare estimates for rows and costs to understand why the planner chose that path. EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the statement and adds measured timings and row counts. This can expose a large difference between estimated and actual cardinality. For a statement that writes data, ANALYZE can cause real changes, so run diagnostics only in a controlled context.

title: PostgreSQL 18: Routine vacuuming
provenance: PostgreSQL Global Development Group, PostgreSQL 18 manual. Project-authored summary checked 2026-11-26.
text: PostgreSQL keeps old row versions after updates and deletes while they can still be visible to transactions. Routine VACUUM makes storage occupied by no-longer-visible versions reusable, and helps prevent transaction ID wraparound. An autovacuum daemon schedules maintenance based on table activity. Ordinary vacuum usually makes space available inside the relation. VACUUM FULL rewrites the table and needs an exclusive lock, so its operational impact differs from ordinary maintenance.

title: PostgreSQL 18: Multicolumn indexes
provenance: PostgreSQL Global Development Group, PostgreSQL 18 manual. Project-authored summary checked 2026-11-26.
text: A multicolumn index stores keys from multiple columns. For a B-tree index, equality predicates on the leading columns and an inequality on the first subsequent column can narrow the portion scanned. With an index on customer_id and created_at, queries that specify a customer and filter by a time range can exploit that ordering. Predicates on later columns may still be checked in the index, and the planner can sometimes use a skip scan. Assess index order against actual query patterns.
